articles.title: Shapiro, Garrity clash on data centers, measles response in Pennsylvania governor debate: 4 takeaways
articles.summary: Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro (D) and state Treasurer Stacy Garrity (R), their parties’ nominees to lead the commonwealth, sparred over an ongoing measles outbreak, voter ID reform and data centers during their first and only scheduled debate on Wednesday evening. The debate was hosted by ABC27, a local affiliate of The Hill’s parent company, Nexstar…
articles.body:
Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro (D) and state Treasurer Stacy Garrity (R), their parties’ nominees to lead the commonwealth, sparred over an ongoing measles outbreak, voter ID reform and data centers during their first and only scheduled debate on Wednesday evening.

The debate was hosted by ABC27, a local affiliate of The Hill’s parent company, Nexstar Media Group, in Harrisburg.

Shapiro has held a strong lead in his reelection race, polling 25 points ahead of Garrity in a Quinnipiac University poll released on Wednesday. The Cook Political Report , a nonpartisan election forecaster, rates this race as solidly in the Democratic column.

Here are four takeaways from Wednesday’s debate:

Each candidate began by defending their stance on data center developments in the commonwealth, amid rising concerns across the country about these facilities’ reported environmental impacts and high energy usage.

As governor, Shapiro unveiled requirements for new data center developments in the commonwealth, but he stopped short of imposing a full moratorium like some other Democratic state leaders .

“I put in place the strictest policy, the strictest guardrails, in the nation to ensure that our communities are protected,” Shapiro said. “Again, just putting it very simply, if a local community does not want that data center to be built in their community, it will not be built.”

Garrity, who has called for a temporary halt of new data center developments in Pennsylvania to allow for more debate on this issue, declined to say during the debate how long she would impose this pause if elected.

“A real leader doesn’t need that long of a pause,” she said. “You get all of the stakeholders around the table, and you find out, what do you need to protect ratepayers and protect communities? So as long as it takes.”

“I come from the private sector, so I think you can get it done very quickly,” she added.

Shapiro refused to address speculation on Wednesday night that he is considering a presidential run in 2028. The incumbent governor has repeatedly sidestepped this question during his reelection bid.

Debate moderator and ABC27 journalist Dennis Owens probed Shapiro on whether he would “serve the full four years as governor” if he was successful in the November election.

“The only thing I am focused on is running for re-election as governor,” he replied. “And I’m focused on these midterms , in trying to generate the kind of turnout and support the kind of candidates who will push back on the chaos, the cruelty and the corruption of Donald Trump, the kind of chaos, cruelty and corruption that my opponent supports.”

When pressed by Owens again, Shapiro pointed to the fact that his opponent would break her four-year term as treasurer if elected governor this fall.

“The treasurer made a commitment she would serve her full term as treasurer,” the governor said. “She’s obviously broken that, and I’m going to do everything in my power to ensure she’s able to serve all four years.”

The two leading candidates traded jabs over the response to a measles outbreak in Pennsylvania. The commonwealth has reported four measles-related deaths this year — a statistic disputed by Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

Garrity has repeated Kennedy’s allegations that Shapiro’s administration hastily linked these deaths to the growing outbreak in an attempt to score political points against the Trump administration. The governor has forcefully pushed back, noting the secretary’s history of vaccine skepticism.

The Republican candidate expressed her support for vaccination against measles and said she believes Kennedy holds the same view. She criticized Shapiro for his response, saying the governor “ran to the camera” before verifying the facts.

“He didn’t get boots on the ground, conduct an investigation and wait to announce, you know, the results, until he had the facts because he is the least transparent governor in modern Pennsylvania history,” Garrity said.

Shapiro countered by seeking to draw a stark distinction between his stance and his opponent and the Trump administration’s perspective on this issue.

“My opponent stands with RFK Jr.; I stand on the side of science,” he said. “Back in the year 2000, measles was eliminated from the United States. It’s come roaring back because of vaccine misinformation and disinformation.”

Garrity and Shapiro also clashed on the issue of voter identification reform — a top issue for the Trump administration.

Several Republican governors have signed new laws requiring voters to present identification when going to cast their ballots amid a stall over a federal bill that Trump has dubbed his “No. 1” legislative priority .

Shapiro said he remained “open” to considering legislation on this issue if it received the support of the commonwealth’s legislature.

“But it can’t be based on the kind of conspiracy theories that my opponent and others continue to this day to spew,” he added.

Garrity expressed her strong support for enacting this legislation in Pennsylvania, saying there was “always some shenanigans” with the commonwealth’s elections process.

“The governor has consistently… used the excuse that he can’t do anything because he has a divided legislature,” she said. “Well, that’s not what real leadership is.”

articles.title: Trump reups beef with ‘ungrateful’ Cuellar for staying Democrat after pardon
articles.summary: President Trump ripped into Rep. Henry Cuellar (D-Texas) Wednesday evening for not switching parties after receiving a presidential pardon in 2025, the latest development in a feud that has intensified since the Democrat announced his reelection bid. In a Truth Social post ahead of a campaign rally in San Antonio, the president said he did…
articles.body:
President Trump ripped into Rep. Henry Cuellar (D-Texas) Wednesday evening for not switching parties after receiving a presidential pardon in 2025, the latest development in a feud that has intensified since the Democrat announced his reelection bid.

In a Truth Social post ahead of a campaign rally in San Antonio, the president said he did not make a “deal” to gain Cuellar’s support in exchange for this pardon — ridding him of federal bribery and money laundering charges — like a “crooked politician would have.”

“But I thought there would be a good chance that Cuellar, who was persecuted by Democrats because they didn’t like him, would have routinely gone over to the Republican Party — The people that saved him from years in prison,” Trump wrote before echoing these points during the rally.

“Shockingly, Cuellar announced, only a few days later, that he is going to remain a Dumocrat,” he continued, using his derogatory nickname for Democrats. “Many considered this to be a tremendous act of disloyalty, and certainly, showed him to be an extremely ungrateful person.”

Cuellar and his wife faced a potential 20 – year prison sentence after they were accused of accepting almost $600,000 in bribes and laundering funds.

Trump pardoned the couple after reading a plea from their daughters. The president also accused the Biden administration of targeting the Democratic lawmaker because of disagreements on border policy.

The Democrat is running for reelection this November in Texas’s 28th Congressional District, which he has represented since 2005. The district, which includes a voting population that is 87 percent Hispanic, was redrawn to favor Republicans in the state legislature’s mid-decade redistricting effort.

The president expressed his support for Cuellar’s GOP opponent, Webb County Judge Tano Tijerina, calling him a “STAR” who he hoped would successfully oust the Democratic incumbent.

“We call that payback for a disloyal and ungrateful person, a person whose life has been saved only to go back into the clutches of the people that tried so hard to destroy him,” Trump wrote. “Henry Cuellar is a LOSER who, right now, should be serving a longterm jail sentence with his wife in a top level penitentiary.”

Federal authorities have charged Cuellar, 68, and his wife Imelda Cuellar, 67, of accepting money from 2014 to 2021 in exchange for the congressman advancing the interests of the former Soviet republic and the Mexican bank in the U.S. He says they are innocent. articles.title: Anti-Israel protesters label Mamdani a 'traitor,' accuse him of 'genocide' outside Oct 7 vigil
articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani was called a "traitor" by anti-Israel protesters who accused him of genocide at an Oct. 7 vigil near Union Square.
articles.body: A group of anti-Israel protesters on Wednesday targeted New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, calling him a "traitor," accusing him of "genocide" and claiming he "cannot weaponize being brown anymore." The crowd of more than 100 demonstrators marched from City Hall to Union Square, where a vigil was held to mark the anniversary of the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas terror attacks in Israel. The vigil was organized as an evening of mourning for those killed in the Oct. 7 attacks and the bloodshed that followed, including Israelis and Palestinians. The anti-Israel crowd was just outside the barricades of the Israelis for Peace Vigil, beating on drums and attempting to drown out the speakers, according to City & State New York. Mamdani was at the vigil and held a candle as protesters threw various insults at him, including accusations of genocide and "selling all your people out." ANTI-ISRAEL GROUPS RALLY ACROSS US ON OCTOBER 7 ANNIVERSARY, CHANTING 'LONG LIVE THE INTIFADA' "Zohran, what do you say? How many kids did you kill today?" the protesters shouted, according to the outlet. "700,000 dead. Mamdani, your hands are red!" they also chanted. "Traitor, traitor, come on out! You sold all your people out!" the group was also heard chanting. The crowd also shouted: "Zohran, you can’t hide. We charge you with genocide!" "We don’t care about where you’re from.
